short: The gap between what stock should have been used and what was.
seoTitle: Food Cost Variance — Meaning, Formula and Example
metaDescription: The gap between what stock should have been used and what was. The gap is waste, over-portioning, theft or mis-costing. Part of the free Setu business glossary.
definition: Food cost variance is the difference between theoretical usage — what recipes say should have been consumed for the dishes sold — and actual usage measured by stock count. The gap is waste, over-portioning, theft or mis-costing.
bodyHtml:
Why Food Cost Variance matters

Food cost percentage tells you there is a problem; variance tells you where it is. It is the difference between a symptom and a diagnosis.

Food Cost Variance formula

Variance = Actual usage − Theoretical usage

Value it at cost and express it as a percentage of theoretical usage.

How Food Cost Variance works in practice

Run it per item on high-value ingredients weekly. A consistent gap on one ingredient points somewhere specific, while a small gap spread across everything usually means the recipe sheets need updating.

Worked example

Sales imply 42 kg of chicken but the count shows 48 kg used — a 6 kg variance worth about ₹1,500 at ₹250/kg.

faq.question: What causes food cost variance?
faq.answer: Over-portioning, waste, unrecorded staff meals, theft, or recipe sheets that no longer match how the dish is made.

faq.question: How often should I measure it?
faq.answer: Weekly on your top few ingredients by value; monthly on everything else.
